- **Never build something that only pretends to work.**
- No new npm dependencies. Server Components by default; `"use client"` only where needed.
- `k-focus` on every interactive element, `k-num` on every figure.
- Must pass `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` on your paths with ZERO errors and ZERO warnings.
- Other agents work in parallel. **Only touch files you own.**

YOU OWN: everything under `app/(portal)/dashboard/new/` and `app/(portal)/dashboard/templates/` (both new). You may READ but must NOT EDIT: `components/marketing/PromptHero.tsx`, `components/templates/TemplateGallery.tsx`, `app/templates/page.tsx`, `app/wizard/page.tsx`, `app/projects/[id]/**`. If you need a shared piece out of TemplateGallery, copy what you need into your own component rather than editing theirs.

## TASK 1 — Create Website (`/dashboard/new`)

This must NOT look like a dashboard page. It is the Kodely homepage AI moment, inside the shell. Minimal, generously spaced, the prompt box is the only real focus.

- Big heading: "What do you want to build?" and a large prompt box, placeholder "Describe the website you want to create…".
- Below it: attach image, use a template, and example prompts as one-tap chips.
- **Attachments — know what is real.** Image attachment IS real end to end: `components/marketing/PromptHero.tsx:44-57` downscales to a data URL, `app/api/generate/route.ts:57-58` validates only `data:image/png|jpeg|webp;base64`, and it reaches the model on attempt 1 only. **Non-image file upload does not exist** — no multipart handling, no object storage anywhere. Do not render a generic "Upload files" control that cannot work. Ship the image path and be explicit about the limit.
- Show the credit cost honestly before they commit — `estimateCredits("create")` from `lib/credits.ts`, and warn if their balance cannot cover it.
- Link to the existing prompt wizard at `/wizard` for people who want help writing the brief.

## TASK 2 — The build-start experience

When the prompt is submitted, do NOT dump them straight into the editor with a blank screen.

Read `app/api/projects/route.ts` (project creation, seeded from `FOUNDATION_FILES`), `lib/pending-prompt.ts` (how a prompt is carried through), and how `app/projects/[id]/Editor.tsx` picks up a stashed prompt and auto-fires the first build. Then design the transition: a Kodely building experience using `AIProgress` with named steps — understanding, planning, designing, generating, content, finalizing.

**CRITICAL HONESTY REQUIREMENT:** `AIProgress` steps must be driven by REAL signals from the generate stream, not a timer walking the list forward. Read `app/api/generate/route.ts` and find out exactly what its SSE event vocabulary is — that file was only partially read during the audit, so **you must read it properly** and report the real event names. If the stream genuinely cannot distinguish these phases, then say so and show fewer, truthful steps rather than six invented ones. A step list that keeps advancing after a build has failed is exactly the fake this redesign exists to remove.

Coordinate: another agent owns `app/projects/[id]/**` and is redesigning the builder's own in-progress state. Your job is the *entry* — getting them from prompt to builder. Do not edit their files; if you need the builder to behave differently, report it to me instead.

## TASK 3 — Templates in the portal (`/dashboard/templates`)

`/templates` is a PUBLIC marketing page and must stay exactly as it is. Signed-in customers need an in-shell version.

- `lib/templates.ts` has 22 hand-written starter PROMPTS in 7 categories. Understand what they are: there is no template file tree, no thumbnail, no preview image, no starting HTML — every project starts from the same `FOUNDATION_FILES` regardless. **Do not present them as visual templates with fake previews.** Present them as what they are: complete, editable briefs. That is genuinely a good thing; sell it honestly.
- Category filtering, search, and a path from a template into your Create flow with the prompt pre-filled and editable.

REPORT BACK concisely: what you built, the REAL SSE event vocabulary of the generate route and how faithfully your progress steps map to it, what was not real, what you deliberately skipped, and anything untested.

11	"build something".
12	
13	---

18	Tailwind class, never a raw hex and never an arbitrary-value bracket.**

61	
62	`k-focus` — **put this on every interactive element.** One focus ring, product-wide.
63	`k-display` `k-h1` `k-h2` `k-label` — the type scale. `k-label` is the only uppercase.
64	`k-num` — **required** on any figure: credits, prices, counts, dates in a column.
65	`k-scroll-x` — wrap any wide table/code block. The page body must never scroll sideways.
66	`k-msg-in` `k-step-in` `k-step-active` — entrance and progress animations.
67	`k-preview-busy` / `k-preview-idle` — the preview treatment while the AI works.
68	`k-wash` — ambient brand glow inside a hero panel. Sparingly: one per page, at most.
69	`k-gradient-border` — gradient hairline. Reserve for the single most important panel.
70	
71	---
72	
73	## Components (`components/ui/`)
74	
75	Import these. **Do not hand-roll a second version of any of them.**
76	
77	| Component | Notes |
78	| --- | --- |
79	| `Button` `ButtonLink` `IconButton` `buttonClass` | Variants `primary\|secondary\|ghost\|soft\|danger`, sizes `xs\|sm\|md\|lg`. **One `primary` per view.** `IconButton` requires `label`. |
80	| `Card` `CardHeader` `SectionHeader` | `interactive` only if it truly responds. |
81	| `Badge` | `tone` + `dot` + `pulse`. Set `dot` on anything conveying live state — colour alone is not a status channel. |
82	| `Input` `Textarea` `Select` `SearchInput` | Label/hint/error/aria wiring is built in. Never hand-write a bare `<input>`. |
83	| `Progress` `toneForUsage` | Recolours as it fills. `indeterminate` for work with no known end. |
84	| `Skeleton` `SkeletonList` | Stagger with `delay`. |
85	| `EmptyState` | `kind` is required: `empty` (none yet) / `no-results` (filter too narrow) / `unavailable` (does not exist yet). These need different sentences. |
86	| `Menu` | Keyboard + Escape + click-outside already handled. `unavailableReason` greys an item and says why. |
87	| `Modal` `ConfirmModal` | Native `<dialog>`. Confirm buttons are labelled with the verb, never "OK". |
88	| `ToastProvider` `useToast` | Provider is already mounted by `AppShell`. Errors and toasts with an action do not auto-dismiss. |
89	| `Segmented` | Real radios. Used for grid/list and device toggles. |
90	| `AIProgress` `stepsAt` | **The** progress component. See below. |
91	| `Stat` `StatRow` | Any number the customer must understand. |
92	| `Avatar` | Initials only — there is no avatar upload. |
93	| `Spinner` | |
94	
95	## Shell (`components/app/`)
96	
97	`AppShell` wraps every portal page and already provides the sidebar, mobile
98	drawer, bottom bar and toast host. **A page renders content only** — no page
99	supplies its own nav, no page sets a background, no page mounts a second
100	`ToastProvider`.
101	
102	Navigation lives in `components/app/nav.ts`. An item may only be added there
103	once it is backed by real data; `soon: true` marks the ones that are not.
104	
105	---
106	
107	## AI progress is one object, not three spinners
108	
109	`AIProgress` is rendered by the initial build overlay, by the chat panel during
110	an edit, and beside the preview. All three must show the **same steps in the
111	same state**, because the customer reads them as one thing happening.
112	
113	**Drive `state` from real build signals.** A timer that walks the list forward on
114	its own is a fake — and it will still be sitting on "Finalizing" long after a
115	build has failed. The build genuinely does not know its percentage (it is an
116	agent loop of unknown length), which is exactly why this is a named-step list
117	and not a progress bar.
118	
119	---
120	
121	## What does not exist (audited — do not build UI that pretends otherwise)
122	
123	| Thing | Reality |
124	| --- | --- |
125	| **Plans / subscriptions** | None. No plan, price, or renewal date. Checkout is one-off `payment` mode for credit packs. **Never render a "Pro" chip or "$X/month".** |
126	| **Credit reset date** | Credits never expire. There is no monthly allowance and no reset day — the spend cap is a *rolling* 30 days chosen so there is no reset. |
127	| **Invoices / payment method** | Not fetched from Stripe. The credit ledger is the only history. |
128	| **Thumbnails** | Nothing captures a screenshot. No headless browser. |
129	| **Project status** | Only `publishedAt` → Published / Draft. No `archived`. "Building" is derivable from `Build.status = RUNNING` but has no staleness rule, so it is not yet trustworthy. |
130	| **Domains** | No model, no field, no route. Sites live at `<slug>.kodely.site` only. |
131	| **Integrations** | Nothing customer-facing. |
132	| **Support tickets** | No ticket model. `SupportNote` is admin-write-only and explicitly never shown to the customer. |
133	| **Storage / bandwidth** | Not measured anywhere. |
134	| **Workspaces / members / roles** | No concept of it. Ownership is one FK: `Project.userId`. |
135	| **Avatar upload, password change, 2FA, notification prefs** | None. |
136	
137	**Sessions list and revoke, and editing `User.name`, ARE cheaply real** — the
138	`Session` model is per-user and queryable.
139	
140	### The rule
141	
142	A screen that looks operable and is not is worse than an absent one. A screen
143	that says "this does not exist yet, here is what you have instead" is neither.
144	Use `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` and say plainly what is missing.

## What I built

**`/dashboard/new`** — `page.tsx` (server) + `CreateFlow.tsx`, `Composer.tsx`, `BuildLaunch.tsx`, `build-steps.ts`, `image.ts`

Not a dashboard page: one `k-display` heading, one large prompt box in a single `k-wash` hero panel, everything else a quiet control under it. Attach-image / "Use a template" / "Help me write it" (→ `/wizard`) as ghost buttons; six one-tap example chips; the credit block last.

- **Image**: real end to end. `image.ts` copies PromptHero's downscale rather than importing it, but *narrows the picker* to `.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp` and re-encodes to JPEG, so the output always matches the `data:image/(png|jpeg|webp);base64,` regex at `app/api/generate/route.ts:57`. Anything else is rejected in the UI with a reason instead of being silently dropped server-side. The panel states the limit plainly: reference images only, first attempt only, no document/ZIP/site upload.
- **Credits**: `estimateCredits("create")` → 120–550 shown as a range with "it is a range, not a quote". Balance ≤ 0 → hard block + billing link (the route would 402 anyway). Balance < 550 → warn that *the balance is only checked when a build starts*, so a build can finish and take them below zero — which is true (`chargeForBuild` just writes `balance - credits`). Spend cap reached / nearly reached → separate callouts linking to `/settings`. `canTopUp` from `billingEnabled()` changes the link label so it's never a dead end.

**`/dashboard/templates`** — `page.tsx` + `TemplateBriefs.tsx`. Public `/templates` untouched. Leads with "These are briefs, not themes" and says outright there is no theme, no layout, no preview behind a card. Each card: name, category badge, honest one-liner, collapsible full brief with a real word count, "Use this brief" → `/dashboard/new?template=<id>` (pre-filled, editable, badged "Started from …"), and Copy. Category chips with counts, search across name/description/category **and prompt body**, `EmptyState kind="no-results"`.

## The real SSE vocabulary of `/api/generate`

Six shapes reach the client: `text` (prose deltas), `progress`, `status`, `file{path,action}`, `done{credits,remaining,filesWritten,buildId,repairAttempts,repairWaived,waivedCredits}`, `error{message}`. **`usage` is produced by the agent but consumed server-side for billing and never forwarded** — the client cannot see spend while a build runs.

The two text channels have enumerable producers:
- `progress` ← `narrateTool()`: `Writing …` / `Writing a file`, `Updating …` / `Making an edit`, `Removing …` / `Removing a file`, `Looking through the project`, `Running a command`; plus `Picking out icons and artwork` (agent.ts:411) and `Compiling the site` (route:305, direct send, bypasses the dedupe).
- `status` ← only two: `Building your site…` / `Applying your changes…` (SDK engine, once) and `Build didn't compile — fixing it…` (route, per repair).

## How faithfully the steps map

**The six requested steps are not supportable.** The stream carries no planning marker, no designing marker, and cannot separate layout work from copy work — a write to `Hero.tsx` is one `file` event either way. Four of six would have been invented. So there are **five**, each with one observable trigger:

| Step | Completed by |
|---|---|
| Creating your project | `POST /api/projects` returns an id |
| Sending your brief to Kodely | `POST /api/generate` answers 200 with a body — i.e. kill switch, balance, spend cap and rate limit all passed and a Build row exists |
| Reading the brief and the starter files | first write evidence: a `file` event, or a `progress` line matching `/^(Writing\|Updating\|Removing\|Making an edit)\b/` |
| Writing your site's files | `progress === "Compiling the site"` |
| Compiling the site | `done` |

`status: "Build didn't compile…"` moves the list **backward** to *Writing* and increments a real repair counter (with "repair passes are not charged" — verified against `settleBuild`). `error` freezes the list and marks the step it died on `failed`. A stream that closes without `done`/`error` reports a dropped connection, never "finished". The verbatim latest `progress`/`status` line is rendered under the list as the raw signal.

The mapping lives in `build-steps.ts` as a pure reducer with no clock access — it *cannot* self-advance. I compiled it and ran a scripted event sequence (happy path, one repair, pre-stream refusal, mid-build error, lost stream, post-terminal frames): all correct, including the backward repair move and the terminal lock.

**Architecture note:** the launch screen runs the real build and only `router.push`es to `/projects/<id>` on `done`. Navigating mid-stream closes the response body → `cancel()` → server-side abort, so any "narrate here, hand over immediately" design would kill the build it was narrating. I abort on unmount deliberately, so "leaving stops the build" is true rather than hopeful, and say so on screen alongside a real Stop button.

## For you to route to the builder agent

1. **No double-fire.** `Editor.tsx:565-581` auto-fires on `PENDING_PROMPT_KEY` when `isFirstBuild`. I never write that key and the build is already complete on arrival (`messages.length > 0`), so there is no double charge from either guard.
2. **`BuildingOverlay.tsx` overlap.** From my entry path the builder's first-build overlay will now almost never be seen — the first build finishes before navigation. Someone should decide whether that overlay is now edit-only.
3. **Retry semantics.** The route writes the user `Message` row *before* running, so a retry after a mid-build failure would be classified `kind: "edit"` against a half-built site. I therefore only offer "Try again" when the server refused with a non-2xx (nothing written, nothing charged); otherwise the failure screen sends them into the builder and says why.
4. `lib/templates.ts` has **23** templates in 7 categories, not 22. My UI counts the array, so it's right either way.

## Not real / skipped

- No non-image upload control of any kind. No thumbnails, previews, or starting HTML on the templates page.
- No live cost/token readout during a build — `usage` never reaches the client. Only the final `credits`/`remaining` from `done`.
- No cross-page nav guard: `beforeunload` covers tab close/reload, and unmount aborts, but I can't intercept a sidebar click to ask first.
- Didn't touch `PromptHero.tsx`, `TemplateGallery.tsx`, `/templates`, `/wizard`, or `app/projects/**`.
